text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on qwen2.5 after the autokernel rollout in eu-west-1. p95 shot up and KV-cache invalidations spiked. attaching quick profiler summary.

sam: ugh, saw alerts. how bad?

maria: p95 from ~120ms -> ~380ms on short prompts. KV invalidation rate increased ~15x for sessions that use mixed CJK+latin inputs. GPU mem +18%. flame snapshot: 
```
p95: 380ms (+260ms)
hot: attention_kernel::fused_matmul_v2 
kvcache_invalidations: 15x (prefix misses)
gpu_mem: +18%
```

lee: interesting pattern — we saw token boundary churn with the tokenizer change last week for mixed-language inputs. that can cause different prefix hashes and trigger cache misses.

jess: can you paste repro curl? want to try local.

maria: reproduce with short script (prod payload obfuscated):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"qwen2.5","input":"你好, this is a test: こんにちは world"}'
```
The interesting bit: when kernel_selector.autotune picks `fused_matmul_v2` we see the invalidations. When we manually force `legacy_matmul` the p95 returns to ~130ms.

arjun: I dug into selector heuristics: autotuner flips kernel if throughput estimate > threshold but it also toggles a small ropescale path optimization that changes how we compute cached KV keys (we missed a normalization step). So two simultaneous diffs: kernel order + ropescale normalization.

sam: that explains why it's CJK-heavy — ropescale normalization interacts with tokenizer boundaries. If tokenization shifts, cached prefix hashes differ.

maria: proof: ran A/B on a replica pool with `kernel_selector.mode=manual` pinned to `tensorcore_v1` and `ropescale=1.0` => invalidations back to baseline, p95 near prior.

lee: Proposed quick mitigation: revert autokernel rollout for qwen2.5 (eu-west-1) and add a gate to prevent ropescale-changing optimizations unless flagged.

jess: Also add an integration test: reproduce mixed-lang sequence, assert kvcache_invalidation_rate < 0.01 under burst load.

maria: Agreed. Plan I pushed to infra: 
1) rollback autokernel for qwen2.5 in eu-west-1 (in progress)
2) add kvcache key normalization in kernel switch path (hotfix)
3) add unit test for tokenizer boundaries + kvcache
4) canary new autokernel with `rope_norm_check=true` only after tests

infra-bot: deploy rollback started for service redwood-qwen2p5-eu-west-1 (deploy id: dpl-8921). ETA ~7m. :rotating_light:

devops-bot: perf-alert cleared on node pool rp-12 after rollback. Monitoring for 30m.

arjun: for the followup, I have a minimal repro harness (python) that forces random token boundary shifts to catch this. Will open PR with harness + fix for kvcache key normalization.

sam: double-check batching heuristics too — autokernel sometimes changes op fusion which increases instantaneous tokens-per-batch and pushes the sampler into a different batching bucket; that can increase tail latency. maybe limit `max_batch_tokens` in selector to avoid sudden bucket jumps.

maria: noted. adding to the action items: add selector constraint `max_batch_tokens: 4096` and `batch_bucket_window_ms: 8` for qwen2.5 until autotuner stabilizes.

jess: will own tests + rollout checklist. tagging @arjun for PR review.

arjun: on it. PR will include: kvcache-normalize patch, test harness, and a small opt-out flag for ropescale heuristics.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: add a dashboard panel for `kvcache_invalidations` per-model and a regression alert if >3x baseline. Also, add an entry in the postmortem tracker.

sam: +1. good catch, maria. :thumbsup:
